nodes.question: How does the paper categorize alternative currencies in terms of their purpose?
nodes.answer: The paper categorizes alternative currencies as monetary devices aimed at transforming territories and society for socio-economic transformation.
nodes.paragraph: "The degrowth movement") before outlin- ing convergences and tensions among perspectives on alter - native currencies within the movement (Sect. "Degrowth and alternative currencies "), including those relating to digital forms of alternative currencies (Sect. "Perspectives on digital currencies"). We next propose questions for future research that debates within the degrowth movement high- light as relevant to a better understanding of the role and design of alternative currencies and monetary systems in socio-ecological transformations (Sect. "Towards a prospec - tive research agenda"). The paper ends with reflections and conclusions (Sect. "Conclusions"). Alternative or complementary currencies? We use the adjective alternative to describe currencies that aim to transform territories and make society , to use the French subtitle of Marie Fare's (2016) book. According to Blanc (2018), alternative currencies are first and foremost monetary devices that are conceived with a view to socio- economic transformation. The use of the adjective socio- economic implies for Blanc that these devices assemble a variety of tools and rules to guide the practices of users in order to achieve an ethical project Of course, there are other qualifiers in the universe of currencies with a voca- tion of socio-economic transformation.
